summary: weekday returns an integer from zero through six, with Monday as zero and Sunday as six.
documentation: weekday returns an integer from zero through six, with Monday as zero and Sunday as six. It operates on a calendar date rather than a time instant, so there is no timezone conversion involved in classifying a supplied date.
inputs: A list of valid YYYY-MM-DD calendar-date strings.
caution: isoweekday uses one through seven instead. A calendar date has no time zone; converting timestamps to local dates should happen separately before using this method.
scenarios: Assign dated tasks to weekday columns in a planner.
Separate weekday and weekend service dates in a report.
Generate local scheduling labels from explicit business dates.
title: Classify calendar weekdays
problem: Parse each valid YYYY-MM-DD string as a date, then return its weekday number using Monday=0 and Sunday=6. Preserve order; invalid strings are outside this problem.
goal: Use date.weekday() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
